description: Somos un equipo creativo que quiere desarrollar un videojuego de supervivencia espacial, donde los jugadores deberán administrar recursos, superar desafíos y sobrevivir en el espacio para encontrar la manera de regresar a la Tierra.
summary: This website helps map routes between various points and determines their difficulty level. It also has several layers that display different information such as elevation, map, temperature, and more. It's important because it would help Mars explorers have a guide for the area they're going to.
details: Our project is a map of Mars that shows data from different NASA missions in one place. We made it for the Martian Map challenge, where the goal is to help a future astronaut plan a walk on the surface. You can choose between Jezero Crater and Gale Crater, and then turn layers on and off. The first layer is a Viking color picture of the surface. The second one is elevation data from MOLA, which was on Mars Global Surveyor. The third one is THEMIS infrared imagery from Mars Odyssey, which shows relative temperature, so brighter areas are warmer. There is also a slider to change the transparency, so you can mix the layers and compare the same place in different ways. After that, the user can click on the map to draw a route. The page calculates the distance using the radius of Mars, not Earth, and gives an estimated walking time in a space suit. It also shows a simple risk level and some safety notes about the place, like the cold and the low gravity, which is about 38 percent of Earth's gravity. We think this is useful because information about Mars comes from many different missions, and it is hard to look at all of it separately. Having it in one view makes planning easier and faster, and it is simple enough that someone without a technical background can understand it. We hope it shows how NASA's open data can work together to help explorers decide where and how to walk safely. It could also be used in classrooms to teach about Mars. To build it we used HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the Leaflet library for the map, and the NASA Mars Trek tile services for the three layers. It runs in a web browser and we published it with GitHub Pages, so nobody needs to install anything. What we liked most about our idea is that we tried to think like an astronaut and not just show data. The main question of the project is whether a certain walk is a good idea or not, and the map tries to help answer that. When we made it, we thought about which data to combine, which places to use, and how to keep the page easy to use. We also know it has limits. Right now the risk level is only an estimate based on the walking time, and THEMIS shows relative temperature, not exact degrees. In the future we want to read the elevation along the route to calculate the slope and warn about steep or dangerous parts.
